newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico and Chile to extend free-trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Mexico and Chile to extend free-trade agreement.

text.p: Mexico and Chile have agreed to expand their free-trade agreement, the Mexican Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Monday.
Talks to expand the accord, in force since 1992, came as part of a meeting begun Monday between Mexican and Chilean foreign ministers Angel Gurria and Jose Insulza, respectively.
Although most goods between both countries are already tariff-free, both sides will seek to make the remaining goods duty free as well, the statement said.
Trade between Mexico and Chile totalled almost $1 billion in 1996, compared to $732 million in 1995, according to official statistics.
